title: Molecular Nanoscale Magnetic Refrigerants: A Ferrimagnetic {Cu15Gd7} Cage-like Cluster from the Use of Pyridine-2,6-dimethanol

synthesis.procedure: Cu(O2CPh)2·2H2O, Gd(NO3)3·6H2O, pyridine-2,6-dimethanol, and NEt3 were reacted in a 1:1:1:1 molar ratio in MeCN under aerobic conditions. The resulting blue suspension was filtered; slow evaporation of the pale-blue filtrate at room temperature produced blue crystals after 10 days.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction followed by filtration and slow solvent evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: The suspension was filtered and the filtrate slowly evaporated to yield blue crystals.

properties.summary: The cluster exhibits overall ferrimagnetic behavior arising from competing antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic interactions. Its high magnetization and negligible anisotropy support a low-temperature magnetocaloric effect. The proposed S = 29 field-stabilized spin state is tentative, not a definitive ground-state assignment.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A cage-like Cu15Gd7 core composed of fused triangular units. A central μ6-carbonato-bridged Cu3Gd3 unit joins three additional Gd ions through μ5-carbonato bridges to form an inner Cu3Gd7 subcore; hydroxido and alkoxido bridges connect this subcore to three peripheral Cu4 units.
